items.title: Alan Broadbent interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 26, 2023
items.q: The name 'Monk' appears exclusively as a form of address for the interviewer (e.g., 'Well, Monk, I don’t.', 'Thank you, Monk.'), not as a reference to the jazz composer Thelonious Monk.

ctx.x: Nice history. Arranging is hard to define sometimes but when you’re presented with a commission or a job or simply curiosity, to arrange something that is a common well known tune — I’m thinking — I wasn’t going to get to Paul McCartney right away but I was struck by the fact that you were involved in that record “Kisses On The Bottom” and you did the chart on “My Valentine,” one of his. But you also did one on “Bye Bye Blackbird.” So my question is, when you’re presented with this task of a well known tune, how…

Well, Monk, I don’t. I was invited by Diana Krall, who was involved in producing this album with Paul. And I’ve known Diana since she was like 19. She studied with me one summer when she came down from Canada. And so we’ve had a wonderful professional relationship in all that time. So she and Paul and her rhythm section had already put down the tracks. And Tommy LiPuma — a wonderful, wonderful guy — basically didn’t want me somehow to get in the way. And I know exactly when he meant is that what they need is not…

An Alanism, yes. That takes a lot of — a certain attitude, some restraint, and as you said there’s a craft in that as well, to be satisfied that you’ve added a small bit that makes the whole that much better.
